newsitem.title: CANADA: Prairie crop output seen a record despite snow - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Prairie crop output seen a record despite snow - CWB.

text.p: Canada's Prairie harvest should produce a record volume of grains and oilseeds despite snow that fell on the region in recent days, a Canadian Wheat Board weather analyst said.

"I still think there's a record volume of grain out there and I don't think it'll (snow) cut it down to the old record. It might just take some of the edge off," CWB director of weather and crop surveillance, Paul Bullock said.
The CWB on Sept 12 forecast Prairie total production of wheat, barley, canola, oats, flax and rye to reach 52.8 million tonnes. The last output record was 51 million tonnes in 1986.
Harvest was stalled for one to three weeks this year by cold, wet weather.
Alberta's harvest was 50 percent complete, Saskatchewan combined 53 percent of crops and Manitoba had 75 percent of crops in the bin by Sept 30, provincial crop reports said.
Between 1.5 and 12 inches of snow had fallen over the Prairies by early Wednesday with low temperatures ranging from 0 degrees Celsius (32 F) to -13 C (8.6 F), Environment Canada said.
"The best face I can put on it is the heaviest snowfall was in the south around Calgary, Regina where the harvest was most advanced," Bullock said.
"This is very bad news for wheat quality and barley quality as well. Before this snow we had problems with bleaching and sprouting," he said.
Alberta was expected to see temperatures in the high teens C on Friday with little precipitation, he added.

"If stuff lays on the ground and is wet and then gets some heat on it, that's perfect sprouting conditions and in terms of quality, that's the worst thing that could happen so it's not a very good prospect that we're looking at here," he said.
